data.title: Live Energy Minerals Completes Issuance of First Tranche of Shares for Plaster Rock Property in New Brunswick
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 30, 2026) - Live Energy Minerals Corp. (OTC Pink: GTREF) ("LIVE" or the "Company") announces that, further to its news release dated October 20, 2026, it has issued 120,000 common shares (the "Option Shares") to an arm's length optionor (the "Optionor") under the option agreement dated October 15, 2026 (the "Option Agreement"). Under the Option Agreement, the Company may acquire a 100% interest in two mineral claims comprising 73 units near Plaster Rock, New Brunswick (the "Plaster Rock Property").

The Option Shares were issued on October 30, 2026 at a deemed price of $0.20 per share, for a total deemed value of $24,000. This is the first share payment under the Option Agreement.

To keep the option in good standing, the Company must issue a further 1,000,000 common shares on or before October 30, 2027 and a further 2,880,000 common shares on or before October 30, 2028. Each later tranche will be priced at the closing price on the last trading day before issuance, subject to the pricing policies of the CSE. The option carries no cash payments and no minimum exploration expenditures. When the option is exercised, the Optionor will keep a 2% net smelter returns royalty. The Company may buy back one-half of the royalty (1%) at any time for $500,000.

The Option Shares are subject to a statutory hold period expiring on March 1, 2027 pursuant to applicable Canadian securities laws. No finder's fees were paid.

About LIVE Energy Minerals Corp.

The Company is a Canadian-based exploration company focused on the acquisition, exploration, and development of North American mining projects. The Company holds the rights to the Mesa Top Mine and Section 20 uranium claims in McKinley County, New Mexico, USA and an option to acquire a 100% interest in the Plaster Rock uranium-copper property in New Brunswick. The Company's McDermitt Lithium East Project in Nevada, USA is under option to US Critical Metals Corp., with the Company retaining a net smelter returns royalty.

data.title: First Atlantic to Acquire 100% of the North Arm Project, 52 sq km of Mantle-Derived Ultramafic Rocks in Western Newfoundland Never Systematically Tested for Geologic Hydrogen, Chromium or Awaruite Nickel-Cobalt Alloy
data.description:
Grand Falls-Windsor, Newfoundland and Labrador--(Newsfile Corp. - October 30, 2026) - First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) ("First Atlantic" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has entered into an asset purchase agreement dated October 30, 2026 (the "Agreement") with two arm's length parties (together, the "Vendors") to acquire a 100% interest in three mineral licences comprising 209 mineral claims spanning approximately 52.25 square kilometers located in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador (the "Property" or the "North Arm Ophiolite Property") (the "Transaction").

The North Arm Ophiolite Property, in the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex ("BOIC") of western Newfoundland, is prospective for geologic hydrogen, awaruite nickel alloy (Ni₃Fe), copper, platinum group elements (PGEs) and chromium. The Property covers mantle-derived dunite and peridotite rocks, the same type of iron- and magnesium-rich ultramafic rocks that host First Atlantic's awaruite discoveries at the Pipestone XL Project. They also enable serpentinization, the water-rock reaction that produces natural (white) hydrogen. Elsewhere in the BOIC, at the Tablelands, active hydrogen-bearing alkaline springs show that the process is happening today. The same rocks are also targets for stimulated (orange) hydrogen and mineral carbon storage (CO2 Capture). Awaruite forms under the strongly reducing, hydrogen-rich conditions that serpentinization creates, making it both a nickel-cobalt target and an indicator of hydrogen generation. The mantle section also hosts podiform chromite, the same deposit style as the historic high-grade chromite occurrences at Blow Me Down and Springers Hill. Numerous historic high-grade chromite occurrences have been found throughout the various ophiolite packages of the BOIC, yet little metallurgical or mineralogical work has been done to examine potential recovery and processing methods. The North Arm Ophiolite Property has seen limited modern exploration and has not been systematically tested for hydrogen or awaruite (a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy).

The Property consists of three mineral licences totalling 209 claim cells (5,225 hectares), on the north shore of North Arm, Bay of Islands. Boats can land directly on the Property, and the nearest road comes within 5 km of it. The claims cover the North Arm Mountain massif, one of the four massifs of the Lower Ordovician BOIC. The BOIC is one of the best-preserved sections of oceanic crust and upper mantle in the world. The North Arm Ophiolite Property lies 25 km north of the Company's Ophiolite-X Project, which covers the Blow Me Down and Lewis Hills ophiolites, and extends FAN's control of ultramafic ophiolite complexes in Atlantic Canada to a third BOIC massif.

Terms of the Transaction

Under the Agreement, the Company will acquire the Property in exchange for the issuance of 1,000,000 common shares of the Company (the "Payment Shares") to the Vendors, at a deemed price of $0.55 per share.

On closing, the Company will also reimburse the Vendors for $51,250 in refundable security deposits previously posted with the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador in respect of the Property. The Company will receive the benefit of any future refund of those deposits.

The Property is free of any royalties or options.

Closing is subject to acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV") and is expected to occur five business days after TSXV acceptance, and in any event by January 31, 2027. The Payment Shares will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

No finder's fees are payable in connection with the Transaction.

The Company also announces that it has granted incentive stock options ("Options") to purchase an aggregate of 950,000 common shares of the Company (each, a "Share") to directors and an investor relations consultant of the Company under the Company's Omnibus Long-Term Incentive Plan which was re-approved by Shareholders on August 13, 2026. The Options can be exercised at $0.55 per Share for a term of five years. The Options granted to the investor relations consultant vest in stages over twelve months, with no more than one-quarter vesting in any three-month period, in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange. The Options, and any Shares issued on their exercise before March 1, 2027, are subject to a four-month hold period.

INVESTOR INFORMATION

The Company's common shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "FAN", on the OTCQB under the symbol "FANCF", and on several German exchanges, including Frankfurt and Tradegate, under the symbol "P210". Investors can get updates about First Atlantic by signing up to receive news via email and SMS text at www.fanickel.com.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

First Atlantic Investor Relations, Robert Guzman. Tel: +1-844-592-6337 | Email: rob@fanickel.com

QUALIFIED PERSON

Adrian Smith, P.Geo., a director and the Chief Executive Officer of the Company, is a qualified person as defined by NI 43-101. The qualified person is a member in good standing of the Professional Engineers and Geoscientists Newfoundland and Labrador (PEGNL) and is a registered professional geoscientist (P.Geo.). Mr. Smith has reviewed and approved the technical information disclosed herein.

ABOUT FIRST ATLANTIC NICKEL & COBALT CORP.

First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) is a critical mineral exploration company in Newfoundland and Labrador developing the Pipestone XL Nickel-Cobalt (Ni-Fe-Co) Alloy Project. The project spans the entire 30-kilometre Pipestone Ophiolite Complex, where multiple zones, including RPM, Alloy Max, Super Gulp, Atlantic Lake and Chrome Pond, contain awaruite (Ni₃Fe), a naturally occurring magnetic nickel-iron-cobalt alloy of approximately 77% nickel with no sulphur and no sulphides, along with secondary chromium mineralization. Awaruite's sulphur-free composition removes acid mine drainage risk, while its magnetic properties enable processing through magnetic separation and flotation, eliminating the electricity requirements, emissions and environmental impacts of conventional smelting, roasting or high-pressure acid leaching, while reducing dependence on overseas nickel processing infrastructure.

The U.S. Geological Survey recognized awaruite's strategic importance in its 2012 Annual Report on Nickel1, noting that these deposits may help alleviate prolonged nickel concentrate shortages since the natural alloy is much easier to concentrate than typical nickel sulphide. In 2026, initial metallurgical test work using the Company's ONSHORE MAX™ (Magnetic Alloy eXtraction) process upgraded RPM Zone material into a high-grade alloy concentrate averaging 67.4% nickel and grading up to 71.9% nickel and 1.76% cobalt, demonstrating a smelter-free, mine-to-refinery pathway. First Atlantic is a member of the U.S. Defense Industrial Base Consortium. The Company is also advancing a parallel geologic hydrogen initiative at Pipestone XL, where the same serpentinization process that formed awaruite also generates natural hydrogen, and has signed a letter of intent with VEMA Hydrogen to jointly develop low-carbon Engineered Mineral Hydrogen (EMH) through a proposed 50/50 joint venture. The Pipestone XL project is located near existing infrastructure with year-round road access and proximity to hydroelectric power, providing favorable logistics for exploration and future development and strengthening First Atlantic's role to establish a secure and reliable source of North American nickel and cobalt production for the stainless steel, electric vehicle, aerospace, and defense industries. This mission gained importance when the U.S. added nickel to its critical minerals list in 2022, recognizing it as a non-fuel mineral essential to economic and national security with a supply chain vulnerable to disruption.

data.title: Crypto exchanges call for quick moves to bolster defenses after Binance heist
data.description:
Key points:
  • Record hack at Binance shows urgent need to address crypto security, industry executives say
  • Trump administration's moves to integrate crypto with financial system raise stakes in big hacks
  • Security experts suspect social-engineering attacks, sophisticated money laundering involved in hack

By Hannah Lang

Crypto exchanges are taking quick action to bolster their defenses and urging greater industry-wide information-sharing after a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance exposed their vulnerability just as they become more embedded in mainstream finance.

Coinbase said it made adjustments to its systems that store cryptocurrency keys offline "solely out of an abundance of caution," while Kraken said it was monitoring industry incidents for lessons it could apply to its defenses.

But the industry will need to move urgently, analysts and industry executives said, as President Donald Trump's regulators promote deeper integration of digital assets into the financial system, raising the stakes for an industry with a history of big hacks.

"For crypto to reach its full potential, the security situation must be addressed immediately," said Chris Perkins, Franklin Templeton's head of crypto.

Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, halted withdrawals after Thursday's attack — which analysts blamed on North Korea — and said it would use company funds to cover the losses.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on X that the “complex attack” may have begun with a compromised software engineer’s laptop, giving hackers access to systems used to process withdrawals. The company later found additional breaches, while software designed to erase traces of the attack hampered the investigation.

Rival crypto exchanges moved quickly on Friday to shore up their own systems and to reassure customers that their tokens were safe

“Full-time teams at Kraken look for potential vulnerabilities every day,” a Kraken spokesperson said.

Still, even as the industry reeled from the biggest cryptocurrency heist of all time, executives expressed confidence that Binance had sufficient resources to cover the losses and that the hack would not have broader financial repercussions.

Bitcoin fell more than 4% on Thursday while ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, fell more than 5%, although both tokens recovered some of that ground on Friday.

"Our expectation is the industry writ large will actually not suffer material losses, even though Binance is obviously going to have to deal with the exploit directly," said Josh Riezman, chief legal and strategy officer at crypto firm GSR.

The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous attacks blamed on North Korea, according ​to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

North Korea routinely denies involvement in cryptocurrency thefts, and its mission in Geneva did not respond to requests for comment.

HACK INVOLVES SOCIAL ENGINEERING, MONEY LAUNDERING

While much remains unclear, social engineering, a common tactic in which hackers trick victims into revealing sensitive information or granting access to systems, may have been involved in compromising the laptop, security experts said.

Harry Donnelly, CEO of Circuit, a crypto risk infrastructure company, said companies are planning more employee training to guard against social engineering attacks.

In such attacks, hackers race to launder the funds before the exchange detects the breach and token issuers freeze assets. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion linked to Binance, while Circle said it froze $800 million. Bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen because no single entity controls the coins.

Chainalysis said the hackers appeared to be using sophisticated laundering patterns it had not seen before.

On Friday, some crypto exchange executives called for the industry to develop a coordinated hack detection system.

"We need a real-time alert system that allows participants to share information immediately when a hack occurs, coordinate a rapid response, and temporarily freeze suspected stolen funds," said Star Xu, CEO of crypto exchange OKX, in a post on X.

GSR's Riezman added that the Binance hack could spur the industry to act: "As we're at this kind of confluence moment for traditional finance and digital assets, I think it's obviously important that we continue to improve, and I think this, if anything, will be a catalyst for that."

data.title: Stocktwits Biotech Dealmaker: BioMarin’s Fabry Disease Drug Candidate License Dominates Slow Week In Dealmaking
data.description:
Key points:
  • BioMarin (BMRN) signed an exclusive worldwide license earlier this week with South Korea’s GC Biopharma and Hanmi Pharm for HM15421/GC1134A. 
  • Teva (TEVA) completed the acquisition of neuroscience assets from BioXcel Therapeutics through a court-supervised bankruptcy sale.
  • The week marked an extension of a quieter stretch in biotech dealmaking after larger deals in the first half of 2026.

U.S.-listed drugmakers continued to prefer asset licensing and bankruptcy purchases of drug candidates this week rather than large full-company acquisitions, marking a quieter stretch compared with earlier in 2026, when multi-billion-dollar buyouts of U.S. biotechs dominated.

This week, rare-disease enzyme therapies and late-stage neuroscience assets drew the most capital as BioMarin and Teva sought to strengthen their positions in certain clinical areas.

BioMarin Licenses Long-Acting Fabry Therapy

BioMarin (BMRN) signed an exclusive worldwide license earlier this week with South Korea’s GC Biopharma and Hanmi Pharm for HM15421/GC1134A, an investigational long-acting enzyme replacement therapy for Fabry disease, a rare disorder that causes a fatty substance to build up inside cells and blood vessels.

BioMarin is paying $70 million upfront. The Korean partners are jointly eligible for up to $405 million in further milestones plus tiered royalties. The candidate is in an early-stage trial and is designed for subcutaneous dosing. BioMarin will lead subsequent global development and commercialization outside Korea.

The licensing deal reflects BioMarin’s efforts to build a pipeline aimed at Fabry, after its acquisition of Amicus Therapeutics was completed earlier this year. The previous deal brought Amicus’s Galafold, approved for Fabry disease, under BioMarin’s fold.

BMRN stock gained about 5% this week.

Teva Acquires BioXcel Neuroscience Assets

Teva (TEVA) completed the acquisition of neuroscience assets from BioXcel Therapeutics through a court-supervised bankruptcy sale. The deal, announced earlier this week, includes worldwide rights to BXCL501, an investigational therapy under FDA review for potential at-home treatment of agitation associated with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, and the approved hospital product IGALMI. Teva paid $57.5 million upfront and could owe up to $67.5 million in contingent payments tied to regulatory timing and sales milestones.

The purchase supports Teva’s pivot toward innovative neuroscience assets. Earlier this year, the company also acquired Emalex Biosciences for $700 million upfront to gain its neuroscience candidate ecopipam for the treatment of Tourette syndrome.

TEVA stock added about 7% this week.

The Shift In Dealmaking Approach

Earlier in 2026, U.S.-listed buyers deployed substantial capital to fully acquire other U.S. biotechs. Major deals that moved markets included Vertex’s acquisition of Crinetics, AbbVie’s purchase of Apogee, Gilead’s buyout of Arcellx, and others that together pushed total U.S. biotech merger and acquisition value well above prior-year levels by the end of the third quarter. Capital also flowed into large licensing packages, particularly for China-originated assets showing potential in immune-system-mediated diseases, cancer, or obesity.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BMRN was 'neutral' at the time of writing, while sentiment around TEVA was 'neutral.'

data.title: Stocktwits Zero To Sixty: Rivian Raises Delivery Guidance On R2 Demand, Tesla Expands Robotaxi Fleet,  And Ford Advances Low-Cost EV Plans
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rivian raised its full-year 2026 delivery outlook to 67,000–70,000 vehicles from 65,000–70,000 and improved its adjusted core guidance by $100 million at the midpoint.
  • EV giant Tesla, meanwhile, continued expanding its robotaxi service this week, with Cybercabs now accounting for a majority of the company’s authorized fleet in Texas. 
  • General Motors, meanwhile, is looking to develop hybrid versions of its high-volume three-row SUVs in the U.S.—the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia, Reuters reported.

This week’s EV spotlight swung firmly to Rivian, which stole the show with a stronger-than-expected third-quarter beat powered by its new R2 SUV—outshining Tesla’s steady robotaxi rollout and the more incremental affordable-EV updates from legacy names like Ford.

Rivian Delivers Record Quarter As R2 Leads Sales; Hikes Full-Year Delivery Guidance

Rivian reported third-quarter revenue of $2.16 billion, up 38% year over year and ahead of consensus estimates near $1.99 billion. The adjusted loss narrowed to $0.48 per share, better than the roughly $0.56 loss analysts had projected.

The company raised its full-year 2026 delivery outlook to 67,000–70,000 vehicles from 65,000–70,000 and narrowed its full-year adjusted core loss guidance by $100 million at the midpoint, while lowering expected capital expenditures outlook to $1.4 billion–$1.5 billion. The hike in delivery outlook is driven by the strong demand for the company’s new R2 SUV, deliveries of which began in June. The company now expects R2 to represent the majority of total delivery volume in the fourth quarter and has added a second shift at its plant in Illinois to scale production.

CEO RJ Scaringe said Rivian remains on track to hit an autonomy milestone by year-end that would unlock a $250 million tranche of Uber’s planned investment. The Volkswagen joint venture continued to contribute meaningful software revenue in the third quarter, and the first EV model from the joint venture will launch next year in Europe incorporating technology from Rivian.

Tesla Robotaxi Fleet Grows; Cybercabs Surpass Model Ys In Texas

EV giant Tesla, meanwhile, continued expanding its robotaxi service this week. Earlier this week, Texas Department of Motor Vehicles data showed 1,051 authorized vehicles in the company’s robotaxi fleet, with 544 purpose-built Cybercabs now outnumbering 507 Model Ys. The crossover marks a clear shift from earlier in October, when Model Ys still outnumbered the dedicated robotaxi vehicle.

Separately, Italy signaled support for broader European Union approval of Tesla’s Full Self-Driving software aimed at automating several aspects of driving. While individual European Union countries have approved FSD, an EU-wide approval is pending, with Tesla previously pegging it for early 2027.

Ford Advances Affordable EV

Ford CEO Jim Farley said testing of the company’s upcoming sub-$30,000 Fathom midsize electric pickup “completely blew me away,” citing its capabilities and low cost of ownership. The vehicle remains on track for a late-2027 launch, with production of large aluminum unicastings advancing and a new bidirectional charging system designed to reduce home-power costs.

Ford also reiterated its longer-term EV financial targets, still aiming for Model e breakeven by 2029, while reporting improved results from its Model e unit. In Q3 2026, Model e posted an EBIT loss of approximately $1.06–$1.1 billion on revenue of $1.2 billion. That marked a roughly 25% improvement from the $1.41 billion loss in the year-ago quarter.

GM Advances Hybrid SUV Plans

General Motors, meanwhile, is looking to develop hybrid versions of its high-volume three-row SUVs in the U.S.—the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia, Reuters reported.

The company confirmed that it is preparing its Lansing Delta Township Assembly Plant for future hybrid production without providing details on timing or final nameplate details. The move marks a notable shift for an automaker that had largely prioritized pure battery-electric vehicles and previously offered only a Corvette hybrid in the U.S. Hybrids have gained share amid elevated gasoline prices, while GM’s U.S. market share has slipped.

While RIVN clocked 3% this week, TSLA gained 7%, GM 15% and F about 6%.

On Stocktwits, sentiment around RIVN stock jumped from 'neutral' to 'extremely bullish' over the past week, while sentiment around GM slumped from 'extremely bullish' to 'bearish.' Sentiment around TSLA stayed unmoved at ‘bearish’ levels, while sentiment around F stock stayed 'neutral' in the meantime.

data.title: NEXE Innovations Reports Q1 Fiscal 2027 Results and Business Update
data.description:
WINDSOR, Ontario, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NEXE Innovations Inc. ("NEXE", the "Company", "we", "us" or "our") (TSX.V: NEXE) Frankfurt:NX5 , a compostable and innovative materials company, is pleased to announce its financial results for the three-month period ended August 31, 2026 ("Q1 2027").

NEXE grew revenue 10.5% to $133,119 in Q1 2027 from $120,484 in Q1 2026, in a quarter that has, in management's view, been historically seasonally soft for the North American coffee industry, and reduced its net loss 33.7% to $(946,396). During the quarter, NEXE began deliveries to an East Coast fair-trade organic coffee co-operative that previously had no single-serve offering and onboarded a U.S. coffee chain with locations in New York City and Boston. Based on current customer interest and commercial opportunities in progress, management currently expects annual pod volumes to exceed the upper end of the previously announced range of 10 to 15 million compostable coffee pods.

Results for the quarter also reflect higher costs. Gross loss was $(47,552), compared to gross income of $16,453 in the three-month period ended August 31, 2025 ("Q1 2026"), and the net loss improvement was, in management's view, primarily attributable to lower depreciation, including the effect of a change in depreciation estimates.

Q1 2027 Highlights

  • Revenue: $133,119, up 10.5% from $120,484 in Q1 2026, in a quarter that has historically been seasonally soft.
  • Net loss: $(946,396), or $(0.01) per share, an improvement of 33.7%, with total operating expenses down 37.4%.
  • Customers: Deliveries began to Just Us! Coffee Roasters, a U.S. coffee chain was onboarded, and the Company is in discussions with a U.S. brand regarding potential distribution to a national hotel chain.
  • Volume outlook: Based on current customer interest and commercial opportunities in progress, management currently expects annual pod volumes to exceed the upper end of the previously announced range of 10 to 15 million pods.
  • Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, GICs and term deposits of $8,008,095 and working capital of $7,693,960.

"Revenue grew 10.5% in what has historically been a seasonally soft quarter, and we began deliveries to new customers during the period," said Ash Guglani, President of NEXE. "Gross margin in the quarter reflected the costs of onboarding those customers, which we believe may trend lower as volumes build. Our focus for the rest of fiscal 2027 is to convert our commercial pipeline into production volume."

Q1 2027 Financial Results

  • Revenue Growth: Revenue was $133,119, compared to $120,484 in Q1 2026, reflecting repeat orders from existing customers and new customers onboarded during the quarter. Shipments were weighted to July and August 2026. The first quarter has historically been seasonally weak, and management believes coffee sales across the industry typically decline during the summer months.
  • Gross Margin: Gross loss was $(47,552), compared to gross income of $16,453 in Q1 2026, as cost of goods sold increased 73.7% to $180,671 from $104,031. Management believes the increase reflects higher volumes, onboarding costs for new customers, higher packaging costs, a larger share of pods filled with coffee purchased by the Company, $54,742 of non-cash production depreciation (recorded in operating expenses in Q1 2026) and $10,685 of inventory write-downs. Management expects that costs will trend lower as volumes increase, as management expects higher volumes will help absorb fixed costs and support bulk purchasing of materials.
  • Operating Expenses: Total operating expenses decreased 37.4% to $950,956 from $1,520,057, and operating loss before other items improved 33.6% to $(998,508) from $(1,503,604). Depreciation in operating expenses decreased 75.9% to $108,103. Effective June 1, 2026, the Company extended the estimated useful lives of its metered production machinery and changed the depreciation method from straight-line to units of use, which reduced Q1 2027 depreciation by $269,353 relative to the previous estimates. Share-based compensation decreased 94.0% to $13,187 and research and development expenses decreased 67.7% to $33,447. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 7.4% to $790,139, mainly due to higher compensation-related costs and higher legal and professional fees, partially offset by lower management fees, salaries, consulting fees, and advertising and promotion.
  • Net Loss: Net loss improved 33.7% to $(946,396), or $(0.01) per share, from $(1,427,807), or $(0.01) per share, in Q1 2026. The $481,411 improvement reflects lower depreciation, share-based compensation and research and development expenses, partially offset by the gross loss, higher selling, general and administrative expenses, and lower interest income.
  • Balance Sheet: As at August 31, 2026, NEXE had cash and cash equivalents of $3,875,352, investments in GICs of $4,102,743 and term deposits of $30,000, for a total of $8,008,095. Working capital was $7,693,960 (May 31, 2026 – $8,464,675), or $6.0 million excluding $1.7 million of prepayments on manufacturing equipment. Cash used in operating activities was $1,096,265 (Q1 2026 – $760,265), mainly reflecting operating expenditures and working capital movements, including a reduction in trade and other payables and an increase in trade and other receivables.

Commercial Update: Management Expects Annual Pod Volumes to Exceed 15 Million

NEXE supplied partners across retail, office coffee services and online channels during Q1 2027, and the previously disclosed partner transition continued through the quarter. NEXE continues to see increased interest in the compostable pod.

During the quarter, NEXE began deliveries to Just Us! Coffee Roasters, an East Coast fair-trade organic coffee co-operative that previously had no single-serve offering, and onboarded a U.S. coffee chain with multiple locations, including New York City and Boston. NEXE is in discussions with a U.S. brand regarding the potential supply of pods for distribution to a national hotel chain and is procuring materials for a new Canadian client.

Management currently expects annual pod volumes to exceed 15 million compostable coffee pods. NEXE anticipates current finished goods capacity aligns with expected production for the coming months and that capacity could be scaled with limited additional investment, such as larger molds or additional staff. The Company is also evaluating strategic opportunities that management anticipates would accelerate commercialization and enhance shareholder value, including potential partnerships, licensing arrangements, and other capital-efficient growth initiatives.

The Company's unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements for the three months ended August 31, 2026 and related management's discussion and analysis are available on NEXE's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca and the Company's website at www.nexeinnovations.com.

*NEXE Innovations Inc. is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Keurig®. Keurig® is a registered trademark of Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.

**NEXE Innovations Inc. is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Nespresso®. Nespresso® is a registered trademark of Société des Produits Nestlé S.A

About NEXE Innovations Inc.

NEXE Innovations is focused on providing innovative compostable material solutions and packaging to the B2B segment to help businesses achieve their sustainability goals. NEXE Innovations has developed a proprietary and patented compostable material that can withstand heat, pressure, and water. Our flagship product, the NEXE Pod, a BPI-certified compostable coffee pod, showcases our material's durability and is an ideal substitute for plastic. The NEXE pod is compatible with major coffee brewing machines and is manufactured at NEXE's vertically integrated facility based in North America. Discover our innovative approach to sustainability at www.nexeinnovations.com and join our journey on social media @nexeinnovations. #compostablecoffeepods #sustainability #greentech
